limits: Actual Martin repository/branch and Cloud application/environment, database and private bucket details are still needed. No actual Cloud build, resource connection, real administrator or production rollout has occurred.

The adapter and SDK are now installed/pinned. Bucket visibility is externally configured; omitting object ACL headers or denying anonymous access at one API endpoint does not certify all public aliases/domains or infrastructure privacy. The probe intentionally reports bucket_visibility_verified=false.

The explicit probe writes only fictional random-key objects on configured nonproduction S3. Readback/privacy failures return nonzero and attempt cleanup. A deletion failure reports the synthetic relative key for operator cleanup; do not ignore it.

No existing files/rows are migrated, repointed or overwritten. Pinned disk metadata and deliberate legacy location remain. Rescue and verify any old ephemeral files before a populated environment is redeployed or its disk references changed.

The S3 signed-HTTP fixture is a local API-contract implementation, not full R2/AWS. It does not certify actual Cloud credentials, TLS endpoint, bucket aliases, multipart provider limits, replication, backup, load or redeployment continuity.

The clean no-dev build is local PHP 8.4.27 and supplied-lock install/package discovery plus Laravel caches. It is not actual Cloud build/deployment or MySQL/MariaDB acceptance. Existing package versions are unchanged; five new runtime dependencies were added.
Hosted staging/setup and combined reminder scheduling remain off by default; production is blocked. No real learner data, real credentials, external messages or schedule activation used.

Actual browser/mobile/keyboard acceptance, controlled legacy migration, target database/concurrency, identity/onboarding/MFA/mail, employer sharing, whole-history compliance and curriculum/gateway/funding decisions remain separate.
